description: Antares was born with a clear purpose: to transform complex problems into agile, viable, and high-impact technological solutions. Driven by collaboration and quality engineering, we combine critical thinking with technical execution to rapidly validate ideas and deliver results that solve real-world pain points in practice.
summary:
MIDORI is a geospatial decision-support platform that combines NASA orbital telemetry with micro-topographic modeling to solve one of agriculture's most destructive and overlooked problems: water ponding, thermal hypoxia, and terrain-driven soil erosion. Most agricultural monitoring tools treat a farm field as a flat, uniform polygon. In reality, subtle variations in terrain relief—depressions of less than one meter and sloped hillsides—dictate where rainwater accumulates or strips away fertile soil. When heavy rain hits, low-lying micro-basins trap stagnant water (water ponding), starving seeds of oxygen, bogging down heavy machinery, and triggering thermal hypoxia when solar radiation heats waterlogged soil, literally cooking seeds in the furrow.

By fusing NASA SMAP L4, ISS ECOSTRESS, GPM IMERG, SRTM 30m (Topographic Wetness Index - TWI), GLDAS, and GEOS-S2S seasonal forecasts, MIDORI maps exact ponding micro-basins and slope erosion zones before a single seed is planted. It shifts sowing windows to dodge extreme weather, reverse-engineers crop timelines for a dry harvest, generates audit-ready technical PDF reports with GPS coordinates, and delivers cloud-penetrating weekly radar alerts to the farmer's phone. MIDORI turns free space data into field-ready protection, preventing costly replanting and preserving soil health.
details:
The Core Problem: Why Terrain Relief and Water Ponding Break Farms

Every harvest season, farmers lose thousands of dollars not because an entire region failed, but because terrain relief behaves differently across the same field:

  • Micro-Basin Water Ponding (Waterlogging): Subtle topographic depressions (often just 50 cm to 120 cm lower than the surrounding field) act as natural funnels for surface runoff. During intense rainfall, water pools in these basins, cutting off oxygen to germinating seeds and causing root rot.
  • Thermal Hypoxia ("Cooked Seeds"): When intense sunlight follows a heavy rainstorm, shallow waterlogged depressions absorb heat rapidly. Soil temperatures spike above biological limits while moisture remains near saturation (90–99%), creating lethal anaerobic-thermal stress that destroys seed viability within 48 hours.
  • Slope Runoff & Sheet Erosion: Before rainwater settles in the low basins, it accelerates down steeper terrain sectors. Without targeted contour management and biological cover, this runoff strips away tons of fertile topsoil and expensive fertilizers per hectare every year.
  • Machinery Bogging & Replanting Costs: Entering a field with hidden saturated micro-basins causes tractors and planters to slip, compacting the soil and damaging equipment. Replanting a single flooded hectare costs roughly $200 to $250 (R$ 1,100+) in extra seeds, diesel, and machine hours.

What Exactly Does MIDORI Do?

MIDORI acts as a 360-degree orbital agronomist for farmers, consultants, and agricultural cooperatives:

  • Digitizes Micro-Topography & Hydrology: Uses SRTM 30m elevation and Topographic Wetness Index (TWI) modeling to pinpoint exact GPS coordinates where water will pool and where slopes risk severe erosion.
  • Detects Surface & Root-Zone Saturation: Integrates NASA SMAP L4 (0–5 cm surface and 0–100 cm root-zone moisture) with ISS ECOSTRESS land surface temperature to separate normal wet soil from lethal thermal hypoxia zones.
  • Calculates Biological Drainage & Crop Succession: Computes a real-time Biological Drainage Index (0–100) for the selected seed and prescribes deep-rooting succession crops (such as Brachiaria, Black Oats, or Sunn Hemp) to naturally perforate compacted ponding zones.
  • Positions Sowing Outside Climate Extremes: Analyzes GEOS-S2S seasonal projections to shift planting dates away from ponding storms during germination and dry spells during flowering.
  • Automates Technical Prescriptions & Mobile Alerts: Generates a printable Agronomic Technical Report (PDF) containing micro-basin tables and erosion control plans, paired with weekly mobile radar alerts that work even under 100% cloud cover.

How It Works: The 4-Stage Workflow

Stage 01 — Field Diagnostics (Terrain & Soil Drainage): The user searches for any municipality or clicks directly on the satellite map, selects the crop/cultivar, and sets the field area in hectares. MIDORI renders the field polygon alongside color-coded hydrological micro-basins (blue for water ponding, red for thermal hypoxia, amber dashed polygons for slope erosion, and cyan polylines for surface runoff paths). Users can toggle live NASA GIBS satellite layers (Moisture and Land Surface Temperature) and view their Biological Drainage Index and succession prescription.

Stage 02 — Hydro-Climate Risk (Hydrology & Sowing Window): MIDORI cross-references terrain saturation vulnerability with GEOS-S2S seasonal forecasts and GPM IMERG extreme precipitation history (>30 mm events). An interactive risk curve highlights upcoming heatwaves and dry spells, automatically shifting the recommended sowing date by $+N$ weeks into a verified safe window.

Stage 03 — Phenological Planning (Crop Cycle Timeline): Before the tractor enters the field, MIDORI checks live seed-furrow comfort by comparing current SMAP soil moisture and ECOSTRESS soil temperature against the target crop's ideal thresholds. It then reverse-engineers the entire phenological timeline—Sowing, Emergence (VE), Flowering (R1), Maturation (R7), and Harvest (R8)—ensuring the final 7 to 14 days fall within a dry harvesting window.

Stage 04 — Prescription & Telemetry (Agronomic Report & Mobile Radar): With one click, agronomists export a responsive Detailed Technical Report (PDF) featuring 6 NASA sensor readouts, a complete GPS table of every ponding micro-basin (with SRTM elevation, depression depth in cm, and TWI score), an erosion risk table (with slope % and estimated soil loss in tons/ha/year), and actionable soil conservation measures. Finally, the Weekly Mobile Radar uses active/passive microwave sensing (SMAP + GPM) to penetrate clouds, alerting farmers to hold heavy machinery for 48 hours whenever recent rainfall saturates low-lying basins.

Key Benefits, UN SDGs & Sustainable Business Model

  • Environmental Impact (SDGs 2, 6, 13 & 15): Directly advances SDG 2.4 (Resilient Agriculture), SDG 6.4 (Water-Use Efficiency via ECOSTRESS evapotranspiration), SDG 13.1 (Climate Adaptation via GEOS-S2S extreme weather avoidance), and SDG 15.3 (Land Degradation Neutrality by halting hillside sheet erosion and promoting biological soil decompression).
    • Consultant Plan (R$ 290/month): Built for independent agronomists to monitor up to 300 hectares and issue branded PDF technical reports.
    • Cooperatives & Resellers Plan (R$ 1,800/month): Enterprise licensing covering up to 1,800 hectares (~R$ 1.00/ha/month) to protect entire member portfolios.
    • Smallholder Inclusion: Free access for family farms up to 20 hectares. Saving just 3 to 4 hectares from waterlogged replanting pays for an entire year of the platform.

Tools, Coding Languages & Technology Stack

  • Frontend & UI Architecture: React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion (smooth step transitions and dynamic gauge animations), and Lucide React icons.
  • Geospatial Engine & Mapping: React-Leaflet & Leaflet.js for interactive polygon rendering, runoff vector polylines, micro-basin halo modeling, and real-time WMS/WMTS tile overlays.
  • Orbital Telemetry & Data Pipeline: Custom TypeScript geospatial service (nasaService.ts) integrating NASA POWER API, Open-Meteo Elevation/Forecast APIs, SRTM 30m digital elevation derivatives, Topographic Wetness Index ($TWI = \ln(\alpha / \tan \beta)$) calculations, and Growing Degree Days ($GDD$) phenological modeling.
  • Hosting, Deployment & Domain: Hosted on Vercel with continuous deployment from GitHub and custom DNS/SSL configured on Hostinger ([https://midoriantares.online](https://midoriantares.online)).

5. USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI)

We developed the core agronomic logic, hydrological micro-basin equations, and platform architecture as a team, utilizing AI tools transparently to accelerate our workflow:

  • Code Assistance & Responsive UI Optimization: We used Google Gemini to assist in structuring TypeScript interfaces, debugging React-Leaflet map viewport synchronization, and optimizing the responsive mobile layout for the technical PDF report and navigation header.
  • Visual & Pitch Asset Refinement: AI image generation tools were used to format clean comparative benchmark tables for our presentation deck. No NASA logos or restricted branding were generated or altered by AI.
  • Content & Translation Review: AI assisted in refining bilingual interface strings (Portuguese/English toggle) and organizing technical documentation. All scientific parameters, TWI/SRTM thresholds, and agronomic prescriptions were manually verified by the team.

6. NASA DATA

  • NASA SMAP (Soil Moisture Active Passive — L4 Surface & Root Zone Soil Moisture): Used to quantify topsoil saturation (0–5 cm) and root-zone water retention (0–100 cm) across low-lying terrain depressions.
  • ISS ECOSTRESS (Ecosystem Spaceborne Thermal Radiometer Experiment on Space Station): Used to monitor land surface temperature (°C) and daily evapotranspiration ($\text{mm/day}$), identifying thermal hypoxia hotspots in waterlogged basins.
  • NASA GPM IMERG (Global Precipitation Measurement): Provides 12-month cumulative rainfall, extreme storm frequency (>30 mm/day events), and 7-day recent precipitation totals for mobile machinery alerts.
  • NASA SRTM 30m (Shuttle Radar Topography Mission): Powers the Digital Elevation Model (DEM), mean elevation, slope percentage (%), micro-basin depression depth (cm), and Topographic Wetness Index (TWI) runoff modeling.
  • NASA GLDAS (Global Land Data Assimilation System) & NASA POWER API: Supplies historical and near-real-time agroclimatological parameters (solar radiation, surface temperature, humidity, and precipitation flux).
  • NASA GEOS-S2S (Goddard Earth Observing System Subseasonal-to-Seasonal Forecast): Drives the Stage 02 seasonal risk model to shift sowing windows away from multi-week heatwaves, floods, and dry spells.
  • NASA GIBS (Global Imagery Browse Services — MODIS Terra Land Surface Temp & SMAP L4 Tiles): Provides live orbital raster overlays directly inside the interactive map.

7. SPACE AGENCY PARTNER & OTHER DATA

  • Open-Meteo Geocoding, Elevation & Weather APIs: Used for municipality coordinate resolution, high-resolution local elevation sampling, and 7-day operational weather synching.
  • Esri / ArcGIS World Imagery Tile Server: High-resolution optical satellite basemap for visual field boundary delineation.
  • OpenStreetMap & Leaflet Geospatial Library: Open-source vector rendering for field polygons, erosion sectors, and hydrological runoff paths.

Antares.
